title: Triangle
summary: Given a triangle array, find the minimum path sum from the top to the bottom.
statement: Given a triangle array, find the minimum path sum from the top to the bottom. At each step, you can move to an adjacent number in the row directly below. Specifically, if you are on index i in the current row, you may move to index i or i+1 in the next row.
constraints: 1–200 rows. Row i has i+1 integers, each between -10000 and 10000.
Start at row 0, column 0. From column i move to column i or i+1 in the next row; reach the final row.
target_time_complexity: O(r²), where r is the row count
hints: The cheapest child today may lead to expensive later rows; use the best complete suffix cost.
Work upward from the bottom row using one row of costs.
For row r and column c, set cost[c] to triangle[r][c]+min(cost[c],cost[c+1]); update columns left-to-right.
Keep a copy of the last row so the input need not be modified; the final answer is cost[0].
editorial: A cell's optimal suffix cost is its value plus the smaller suffix cost of its two reachable children. Initialize costs from the last row and apply this recurrence upward. Left-to-right updates keep cost[c+1] from the row below until it is needed. Negative values are handled naturally because the triangle has no cycles. One row of memory suffices. The independent oracle enumerates every sequence of left/right moves on small generated triangles.

tests.explanation: The adjacent choices 2→3→5→1 sum to 11, the minimum.
The top is already the bottom, so the only path has sum -10.
